To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we introduce multilingual image descriptions, a new task that is useful for visually-grounded machine translations, and (b) we propose models for multilingual image description and demonstrate that they substantially outperform monolingual image descriptions on the new task.

(1) multilingual image description is a useful task for visually-grounded machine-translation; (2) our multilingual image description model improves upon monolingual image-description models, and; (3) our model is a step in the direction of building a machine-translation model that uses visual features as a source of information.

(1) multilingual image description can be viewed as a form of visually grounded machine translation, (2) multilingual image descriptions can be generated using a model that transfers features from separate models: monolingual source language image descriptions and a visual model, (3) the resulting models improve upon existing monlingual image description models, and (4) the results suggest that the image plays a role in disamibiguating language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the task of multilingual image description and the models we present for this task.
two problems: (i) how to generate descriptions of images in a target language given data in multiple other languages, and (ii) how to transfer features between monolingual and multilingual models.
the problem of image description in the presence of multilingual data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our multilingual image description system outperforms the state-of-the-art in monolingual image descriptions, and is competitive with the state-of-the art in machine translation.
our models achieve a 1.6 BLEU improvement over state-of-the-art monolingual image descriptions, and a 2.4 BLEU improvement over the best multilingual image descriptions.
we introduce the task of multilingual image description and present a novel model architecture that improves over the state of the art for monolingual image captioning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural models for image and video description are well suited to the task of generating visually-grounded machine translated descriptions.
multilingual image description is a promising direction for future research, and that neural sequence models can be used to address it.
multilingual models can be trained to generate descriptions of images in multiple languages by using separate models for the source language and the target language.
